question.text: Can an officer who has conducted an investigation or inspection in respect of an alleged violation be appointed as a designated authority under SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008?

answer.text: Yes, but only if no other officer is available
No, such officer cannot be appointed as a designated authority
Yes, such officers are preferred due to their familiarity with the case
Yes, with approval from the Executive Director

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, no officer who has conducted the investigation or inspection in respect of the alleged violation can be appointed as the designated authority for the subsequent enquiry proceedings. The Trap: Familiarity with the case may sound like a practical advantage, and conditional appointments (only if no other officer is available, or with senior approval) sound plausible -- but the regulation contains a flat prohibition, not a conditional permission. Note: Workbook reference: NISM Series III-C p.99 directly states this disqualification for designated-authority appointments.
